record.paper_title: Dima Khavinson’s 60th: a summary of open problems in analysis and mathematical physics
record.original_question: Let D be a region in R^n with boundary regular for the Dirichlet problem. Consider PI: there exists a bounded nonzero temperature u on D × [0,1] solving u_t = Δu and satisfying u(x,1) = 0 for all x in D. Consider PII: there exists a nonzero harmonic function v on D such that v(x) = O(exp(-|x|^2)) as |x| → ∞. Are PI and PII equivalent for every such region D?

evidence.quote: PI. There exists a bounded temperature function u(x, t) ≢ 0 ... with the property u(x, 1) = 0 for all x ∈ D.
PII. There exists a harmonic function v(x) ≢ 0 in D with the property v(x) = O(exp(−|x|^2)), x → ∞.
According to Gurarii and Matsaev [35], these properties are equivalent, but no proof was ever published.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $D \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ be an unbounded region whose boundary is regular for the Dirichlet problem (every continuous boundary datum admits a classical harmonic extension that attains the data continuously at every boundary point). Consider the following two statements about $D$:

(PI) There exists a bounded function $u : D \times [0,1] \to \mathbb{R}$, not identically zero, that is continuous on $\overline{D} \times [0,1]$, vanishes on $\partial D \times [0,1]$, satisfies the heat equation $u_t = \Delta u$ in $D \times (0,1)$, and satisfies $u(x,1) = 0$ for every $x \in D$.

(PII) There exists a harmonic function $v : D \to \mathbb{R}$, not identically zero, that is continuous on $\overline{D}$, vanishes on $\partial D$, and satisfies $v(x) = O(\exp(-|x|^2))$ as $|x| \to \infty$ within $D$.

Prove or disprove: for every such region $D$, the statements (PI) and (PII) are equivalent.
artifact.category_tag: Backward uniqueness for the heat equation
artifact.status_search_result: The equivalence was asserted by Gurarii and Matsaev but no proof was ever published. Subsequent work (e.g., Lopez-Fernandez, Vondrak, Sverak, and others on backward uniqueness in cones and conical domains, arXiv:1011.2796 and arXiv:1310.6655) addresses backward uniqueness in specific geometries but does not establish the general equivalence of (PI) and (PII) for all Dirichlet-regular domains. The general question appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Backward uniqueness for the heat equation in cones
status_evidence.snippet: Studies backward uniqueness for the heat equation in cones, a special case of the more general problem.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work addresses backward uniqueness only in special geometries, not establishing the general equivalence.

status_evidence.title: On the Backward Uniqueness Property for the Heat Equation in Two-Dimensional Conical Domains
status_evidence.snippet: Investigates backward uniqueness in two-dimensional conical domains.
status_evidence.claim: Continued investigation of the topic in restricted settings indicates the general problem remains unresolved.
